newsitem.title: CHINA: China's elderly population to increase faster.
newsitem.headline: China's elderly population to increase faster.

text.p: One in every four Chinese will be over 60 by the middle of next century as the pace of growth in China's elderly population quickens, Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.
China's senior citizenry is expected to increase to 132 million by the turn of the century, up from a current 120 million, Xinhua said, quoting experts from the Chinese Association of the Elderly.
That figure would climb to 374 million by the year 2040, some 25 percent of the total population, they said.
"The increasing scale of the elderly population in China is probably the largest in the world," it said.

Since 1990, the number of elderly has risen by 3.32 percent a year in big cities such as Beijing, Shanghai and Tianjin. The booming coastal provinces of Jiangsu and Shandong have reported even higher rates of increase, it said.
Better health conditions and higher living standards have resulted in average life expectancy of Chinese doubling to 70 years, from just 35 in 1949.
In Beijing, life expectancy has reached 74 years, Xinhua said.
China's population of more than 1.2 billion is the largest in the world.
